compiled_state.description:
`to_host_url` and `to_host_hostport` in `scripts/config.py:245-280` rewrite a Compose service name to `localhost` but carry the original port through unchanged. That is only correct while every service publishes on the host under the same number it listens on inside the network.

`compose.yaml` hardcodes each published port, for example `ports: ["5432:5432"]` at line 22 and `ports: ["3000:3000"]` at line 301. An operator whose host already uses those numbers must remap them in an overlay. Once remapped, the rewrite produces an address that does not answer. On the pilot machine postgres publishes 15432, so `postgresql://platform@postgres:5432/agent_platform` rewrites to `localhost:5432` and every host-run database tool fails.

The hardcoded ports are the root cause. The rewrite has no way to learn the published number because nothing records it outside the compose file.

Parameterising each published port with an environment variable that defaults to today's value gives both the compose file and the rewrite a single source of truth, and removes the need for an overlay to override ports at all.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A Compose service URL rewrites to the published host port when that port is remapped, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_host_rewrite.py -k host_url_uses_the_published_port_when_remapped`
- [ ] A Compose service URL keeps its port when no remap is configured, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_host_rewrite.py -k host_url_keeps_the_default_port_when_unmapped`
- [ ] A rewritten URL preserves user credentials, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_host_rewrite.py -k host_url_preserves_credentials_across_the_port_remap`
- [ ] A Compose host:port value rewrites to the published host port when remapped, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_host_rewrite.py -k host_hostport_uses_the_published_port_when_remapped`
- [ ] A non-Compose hostname is returned unchanged, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_host_rewrite.py -k host_url_leaves_a_foreign_hostname_alone`
- [ ] The rewrite stays inert inside the platform image, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_host_rewrite.py -k host_url_is_inert_inside_the_platform_image`
- [ ] Every Compose service that the rewrite recognises publishes its port through a variable, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_host_rewrite.py -k every_rewritable_service_publishes_through_a_variable`

## Testing
Run each acceptance criterion selector on its own. Run `PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" .venv/bin/inv ci` before closing the ticket.
compiled_state.title: Rewrite Compose service URLs to the published host port rather than the internal port
